standard_prerequisites.name: Two-term case
standard_prerequisites.use: The base case n = 2 of the induction is exactly Lemma lemma-make-injective, and the induction step applies that lemma to a composition.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 804-812): for any sequence of composable homomorphisms L_1 -> L_2 -> ... -> L_n of differential graded A-modules there is a commutative diagram with vertical maps M_i -> L_i which are homotopy equivalences and horizontal maps M_i -> M_{i+1} which are admissible monomorphisms.
Base cases (proof lines 813-816): the case n = 1 is without content; the case n = 2 is exactly Lemma lemma-make-injective.

Induction step (lines 816-824): suppose the diagram is constructed except for M_n; apply Lemma lemma-make-injective to the composition M_{n-1} -> L_{n-1} -> L_n; the resulting factorization M_{n-1} -> M_n -> L_n, with M_{n-1} -> M_n an admissible monomorphism and M_n -> L_n a homotopy equivalence, supplies the missing column and completes the commutative diagram.
proof_roadmap: Start from the trivial one-term case and the two-term case given by the make-injective lemma.
Induct: apply the two-term case to the composition into the next target.
Assemble the commutative ladder with admissible monomorphisms and homotopy equivalences.
difficulty_reason: Dominating-ladder lemma (statement 804-812, proof 813-824): every composable sequence admits a commutative ladder of admissible monomorphisms under homotopy equivalences - the proof is a complete induction whose mechanism (applying the two-term factorization lemma to the composition) is stated in the span; the workhorse two-term case is delegated to the in-source Lemma lemma-make-injective as a stub; no step is omitted. H2: short induction.
